copies.headline: Noah's 0-3 Floor Meets CJ's Running Game
copies.body:
The gap is on the ground. CJ's best two backs, Jonathan Taylor in a 47.5-total game Indy is favored in, plus Chuba Hubbard against Detroit in a 50.5 shootout Carolina likely loses late, project eight clear of Noah's pair, and that's before you count Quinshon Judkins and TreVeyon Henderson sitting on the bench as real flex options. Noah's RB2 is Rhamondre Stevenson, a 6.5-point underdog in Buffalo where New England will throw and Drake Maye gets the volume, not the handoffs. James Cook is the one back in this game with a clean path to touchdowns.
Receiver is a coin flip on paper — Garrett Wilson, Josh Downs and Michael Wilson vs. Parker Washington, Rashee Rice and Emeka Egbuka — but Noah has nothing behind those three with Jordyn Tyson on IR, so any inactive craters the whole week. That's the story of an 0-3 start and a 2-31 all-play: no margin anywhere. Noah's 79.6, 84.2, 85.2 isn't bad luck, it's the ceiling.

copies.headline: Grant's Receivers Outrun Kaleb's Running Backs
copies.body:
Grant wins this at wideout and it isn't close. Amon-Ra St. Brown in a 50.5-total game at Carolina, Zay Flowers against a Titans team getting 11.5 and throwing all afternoon, and Christian Watson in a 39.5-total slog that Green Bay is favored in by 3.5 — that's 50 from his top three against Kaleb's 40, and Kaleb's WR points come from a committee of 12s rather than a single guy who can go for 30. Jaylen Waddle's questionable tag barely matters when he's the fourth option. Kyler Murray with Minnesota favored by 10.5 in a 38.5-total game is the soft spot; that's a sit-on-the-lead script.
Kaleb's counter is the ground game, and it's real: Ashton Jeanty against Kansas City with a 47.5 total and Las Vegas chasing from 4.5 down is his highest-ceiling asset. But behind Jeanty is RJ Harvey and a questionable Breece Hall, so an inactive there is a hole. Grant's four-deep RB room absorbs a scratch; Kaleb's doesn't.

copies.headline: Isaac's 2-1 Is Paperwork, Not Evidence
copies.body:
Isaac is 2-1 with a 9-24 all-play and 100.1 points per game, 11th in the league — he has won two games he mostly didn't earn, and the schedule is finally done doing him favors. On paper he owns the skill positions: Chase, Nabers and McLaurin beat John's top three receivers by six, and Warren plus Skattebo edge Swift and Kyren by five. The problem is where those points come from. Boswell and the Steelers sit in a 38.5-total slog at Cleveland, the Giants are home dogs, and Kincaid at 11 is a full seven behind Trey McBride before you remember John also has Brock Bowers on the bench.
John scores 120.9 a game, fourth in the league, and has lost twice doing it. Nacua's questionable tag is the swing — Rams at Philly, a 43.5 total and Stafford leaning on him and McBride all afternoon. If Nacua plays, John's receiver gap shrinks to nothing and the tight end edge decides it. If he sits, Wicks and Wan'Dale are a real problem and this gets close. Bet on the better team.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Receivers Are Bringing A Knife
copies.body:
Adam is 31-2 in all-play because nothing on this roster is a hole. The receiver room decides this one: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave and a questionable Jalen Coker project 53 to Mitchell's 41, and Mitchell's third-best option is Matthew Golden or Courtland Sutton depending on the day. Nico Collins is questionable with Tank Dell on IR behind him, so a Friday downgrade leaves Mitchell starting Xavier Hutchinson in a 48.5-total Houston game he'd otherwise be exploiting. Smith-Njigba gets Seattle as a seven-point favorite, which is the one line that mildly concerns Adam — a comfortable lead in a 42.5 total means fewer throws.
Mitchell's path is Jahmyr Gibbs in a 50.5-total game at Carolina, plus Dak Prescott chasing points as a 2.5-point dog in Houston. That's real, but it's two players against a roster with none. Behind Gibbs, Rachaad White at 8 and Jordan Mason on IR isn't depth, it's a formality.

copies.headline: Peter's 3-0 Is A Rental, Not A Deed
copies.body:
The backfields settle this. Leif runs Christian McCaffrey against Denver in a 47.5-total game San Francisco is favored in, plus Derrick Henry with Baltimore laying 11.5 on Tennessee — the exact script where a favorite sits on a lead and hands it off 25 times. Peter has Bijan Robinson, who's fine as a three-point underdog in New Orleans with a 48.5 total, and then a cliff: Kyle Monangai and Kaleb Johnson at 8 and 7, with Josh Jacobs day-to-day and offering nothing. That's a ten-point gap at the position before anyone touches the ball.
Everywhere else it's close enough to call a wash, which is why depth decides it. Peter's receivers are workable — Pickens and Higgins in a 51.5-total Bengals game — but A.J. Brown on IR left no cushion. Leif's swing is Josh Allen's questionable tag; if Allen plays, Peter is depending on a luck rating of +1.5 that's already borrowed.

copies.headline: Someone Has To Win This, Unfortunately
copies.body:
Two 0-3 teams, but only one of them is actually bad. Christian is scoring 127.0 a game, third in the league, with a 19-14 all-play — he's the third-best roster in the Players League sitting on three losses. Logan is 102.0 a game, 10th, and trending the wrong way: 137.2, then 86.4, then 82.5. The lineup math is thin everywhere but receiver, where Logan's 46 to 43 edge is propped up by a questionable Justin Jefferson in a 38.5-total game Minnesota is favored by 10.5 in — a script that means Aaron Jones running out the fourth quarter for Christian, not Jefferson targets.
The leverage is in the shootouts. Christian has Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten and Chase Brown in a 51.5-point Jacksonville-Cincinnati game, plus CeeDee Lamb and Brandon Aubrey in a 48.5. Logan's Hurts-Barkley stack is buried in a 43.5 against the Rams, and behind Jefferson it's Tetairoa McMillan and hope. If Jefferson sits, this isn't close.

intro: The headline game is Leif at Peter, where Peter's 3-0 start meets the only unbeaten-adjacent roster with actual positional depth behind it — Leif is favored, and if that holds, Adam stands alone at the top provided he handles Mitchell, who has lost two straight and can't get consistent production out of the flex spots. The widest gap on the board is Christian at Logan, a game between two 0-3 teams that manages to still have a clear favorite, which is its own kind of accomplishment. Elsewhere, John gets Isaac at home in the week's most consequential middle-of-the-pack game: Isaac drops to .500 with a loss, while John climbs back into the playoff conversation with a win.
